image_description: A close-up, eye-level shot of a Dungeness crab (Cancer magister) resting on a weathered wooden surface. The crab is facing the camera, displaying its broad, reddish-brown carapace with lighter mottling. Its two large chelipeds (claws) are prominent in the foreground, showing white tips and serrated inner edges. Several walking legs are visible extending laterally, though some are obscured by the angle and depth of field. The background is blurred, suggesting a shallow depth of field.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: While not all 10 legs are fully visible due to perspective and occlusion, multiple walking legs are seen extending from both sides, and no structural anomalies (like missing or fused legs) are evident in the visible portions.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The outer surface of the claws appears smooth, and the inner edges (visible where the claws meet) show clear serrations/teeth.

The rearmost walking leg on the right side seems to fade into the background without a clear termination point or joint structure, appearing slightly 'melted' or incomplete compared to the sharpness of the front claws.
